content: 1. Exenatide slows gastric emptying, which may reduce the absorption and effectiveness of oral medications requiring rapid gastrointestinal absorption. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least one hour before exenatide administration. Close monitoring is advised when using exenatide with medications like ethinyl estradiol. 2. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, potentially reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Patients with diabetes should be closely monitored for glycemic control. 3. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and alternative therapies should be considered. 4. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of fedratinib, potentially leading to adverse effects. Avoid coadministration with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors, as the interaction has not been fully studied. 5. Felbamate decreases ethinyl estradiol levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 6. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of desogestrel and ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP2C19 and CYP2E1 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of adverse effects. 7. Fezolinetant levels and effects are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP1A2 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated, as it may lead to significant increases in plasma concentrations. 8. Finererone levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring, including serum potassium levels, are recommended during initiation or dosage adjustments. 9. Flibanserin levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution is advised, as coadministration with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of adverse effects. 10. Fluconazole increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 11. Fluvoxamine levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP1A2 inhibition. Caution is advised, and alternative therapies may be necessary. 12. Fosamprenavir coadministration with ethinyl estradiol may alter hormone levels and reduce virologic response. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 13. Fostemsavir increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid coadministration or modify the dose of BCRP substrates. Ethinyl estradiol doses should not exceed 30 mcg/day. 14. Grapefruit increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 15. Green tea levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol due to decreased elimination. Caution is advised. 16. Griseofulvin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing contraceptive efficacy. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 17. Hemin effects are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution is advised, as drugs increasing delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may further reduce hemin efficacy. 18. Heparin effects are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Hyaluronidase effects are reduced by estrogens in large systemic doses, potentially requiring higher doses of hyaluronidase for equivalent dispersing effects. Caution is advised. 20. Idelalisib increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 21. Iloperidone increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, as iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A4 inhibitor. 22. Imipramine metabolism may be reduced by ethinyl estradiol, potentially increasing antidepressant serum concentrations and adverse effects. Caution is advised. 23. Indinavir coadministration with ethinyl estradiol may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, reducing contraceptive efficacy. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 24. Insulin effects (e.g., aspart, degludec, detemir, glargine, glulisine, lispro, NPH, regular human) are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Close monitoring of glycemic control is recommended in diabetic patients. 25. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Istradefylline increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be considered. 27. Itraconazole increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, as plasma hormone levels may increase. 28. Ivosidenib decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 29. Ketoconazole increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, as plasma hormone levels may increase. 30. Lamotrigine levels are decreased by ethinyl estradiol due to increased hepatic clearance, likely through glucuronidation induction. Close monitoring is recommended. 31. Lapatinib levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution is advised. 32. Larotrectinib increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 33. Lemborexant levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Lower nightly doses of lemborexant are recommended when coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 34. Lenacapavir increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, as lenacapavir may increase the risk of adverse reactions for up to nine months after the last dose. 35. Leniolisib increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Lesinurad decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing contraceptive efficacy. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 37. Letermovir increases desogestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised. 38. Letrozole effects are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 39. Levofloxacin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution is advised. 40. Levoketoconazole increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised. 41. Liraglutide effects are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Close monitoring of glycemic control is recommended in diabetic patients. 42. Lixisenatide decreases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least one hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. 43. Lomitapide levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Lomitapide doses should not exceed 30 mg/day. 44. Lonafarnib levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
